\subsection{Impedance Spectroscopy}\label{ss:eis}

The channel measures impedance with no impedance hardware. A small excitation
rides on the reference-DAC setpoint of Section~\ref{ss:dacr2r12}, A1 applies it
at the reference electrode, A2 and the converter read the resulting current
through the same programmable feedback resistor a dc measurement uses
(Section~\ref{ss:tiarprog}), and firmware demodulates the potential and current
records in quadrature against its own reference. The excitation is a toggle
between two DAC codes, so the mode adds a clock divider and an accumulate to the
channel of Section~\ref{ss:pixtop} and nothing else.

Everything below is on the assembled channel's own netlist at a
\SI{2.5}{\volt} analog supply, and schematic-level except where the converter
appears, which it does as its extracted view. At the nominal process point and
\SI{37}{\celsius}: 30 small-signal runs, five electrode loads against six gain
codes over \SI{0.01}{\hertz}--\SI{100}{\kilo\hertz} at \num{20} points per
decade; 24 runs against pure
resistors chosen to hold the ratio \(R_f/|Z|\) fixed across the sweep; and 17
transient runs in which the twelve potential-code lines are driven individually,
so the excitation is produced by the real ladder rather than by an ideal source.
Twenty points per decade and not ten because at ten the chord through the
plotted points departs the true arc by \SI{0.65}{\percent} of its radius,
twice the instrument's own error there, and at twenty by \SI{0.165}{\percent}
(Figure~\ref{fig:eis-nyquist}).
Through the converter: one record of \num{256} conversions of the extracted
converter, the excitation synthesised by the real reference ladder and both
channels read through the input multiplexer. Across process and temperature:
the small-signal and fixed-ratio runs repeated over the
chapter's four process corners at \SI{25}{\celsius} and over
\SIrange{0}{85}{\celsius} on the nominal models, 252 runs, and again on a dense
grid with the poly ladder and the feedback capacitor cornered as well. Across a wafer: eight
Monte Carlo runs of the small-signal measurement at the nominal corner, six of
\numrange{643}{663} samples with process and mismatch together and two of
\num{500} that separate them, every \(\sigma\) carrying an exact
\SI{95}{\percent} interval. The demodulator is the firmware one --- an
I/Q multiply--accumulate over an integer number of excitation periods, no window,
no detrending. The electrodes are the linear cell model of
Section~\ref{ss:analog-models} with \(R_u = \SI{1}{\kilo\ohm}\) throughout;
\emph{fresh}, \emph{typical} and \emph{fouled} name
\(R_{\mathrm{ct}} \parallel C_{\mathrm{dl}}\) of
\SI{1}{\mega\ohm} \(\parallel\) \SI{100}{\nano\farad},
\SI{100}{\kilo\ohm} \(\parallel\) \SI{1}{\micro\farad} and
\SI{10}{\kilo\ohm} \(\parallel\) \SI{10}{\micro\farad}.

\input{include/analog/fig_eis_nyquist.tex}

\textbf{The pinned-passive caveat of page~\pageref{p:pinned-passives} governs
every corner number in this section.} Neither the ladder that is \(R_f\) nor the
capacitor that sets the feedback pole corners here. Cornering the poly as well moves \(R_f\) by
\(-33.4\,\%\) and \(+35.5\,\%\) and the feedback pole at the top
gain code to \SIrange{2.40}{6.61}{\kilo\hertz}, against the
\(\pm\SI{1.2}{\percent}\) the corner set alone reports. The Monte Carlo does vary
the poly, and measures the same quantity as \(\sigma = \SI{11.1}{\percent}\)
(Section~\ref{sss:eis-accuracy}). It also moves the phase band edge by a factor
of three at a frozen noise gain, which is measured in
Section~\ref{sss:eis-coverage} rather than bounded.
